Retreat Planner Terms
For Retreat Planners | Version 1.0 | 13 November 2026

1. Welcome and who we are
Light Path Retreats is a marketing and booking platform. We help guests find your
retreat. We do not run retreats, and we are not the seller of any retreat.


1.1 These Retreat Planner Terms (“Terms”) are an agreement between you and Light
Path Retreats LLC, a limited liability company registered in New Mexico, USA, of 1209
Mountain Road Pl NE, Ste R, Albuquerque, NM 87110, USA (“Light Path Retreats”,
“we”, “us” or “our”). They apply to retreat planners and retreat leaders (each a “Planner”)
who list or sell a retreat through lightpathretreats.com and related services (the
“Platform”).

1.2 By creating an account and ticking the box that says you have read and agree to
these Terms, you accept them. If you accept for a business, you confirm that you have
authority to bind it. We keep a record of the date, time and version you accepted.

1.3 Venues and facilitators who list on the Platform have their own separate terms. If you
also list a venue or offer your services as a facilitator, those terms apply to that part of
what you do.

1.4 These Terms form one agreement with the Listing Guidelines (Schedule A), the
Acceptable Use Rules (Schedule B), the copyright notice process (Schedule C), and our
Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy, both published on our website. If they disagree, these
Terms come first, then the Schedules, then the policies.

1.5 Guests who book through the Platform are covered by separate Guest Terms. The
contract for a retreat itself is between you and the Guest.

3. What we do, and what we do not do
3.1 We run a marketing and booking platform. We provide the technology, Listings,
messaging, a reviews system, promotion of the Platform, and a checkout that takes the
Booking Payment into the Planner’s Stripe Account.

3.2 We are not a party to any agreement between a Guest and a Planner, or between a
Planner and the venues, facilitators and other suppliers it works with. Those are direct
agreements between the people involved.

3.3 We do not organise, run, supervise, inspect or insure any retreat, or any venue or
supplier a Planner uses. We are not responsible for what happens at or because of a
retreat, including activities, practices, substances, food, accommodation, health and
safety, travel, permits, licences or insurance. Those are the responsibility of the Planner
running the retreat or providing the service.

3.4 How payments work. Payments for retreats are processed in your own Stripe
Account, and you are the seller and the merchant of record. When a Guest pays the
Retainer or the Full Payment, Stripe sends our 15% Commission to Light Path Retreats
at that moment, as a platform fee. The rest of the payment goes straight into your Stripe
Account, less Stripe’s fees, and is paid out to you on your Stripe payout schedule. Light
Path Retreats does not hold the rest of the payment, is not your payment agent and is
not the seller of any retreat. If a Guest cancels within the Cancellation Window, the
refund is made from your Stripe Account and we return our Commission to it, less €30
(clause 5.14), so until the window has closed, keep enough in your Stripe Account to
cover a refund.

3.5 We may decline, hide or remove any Listing at our discretion, including where a
payment provider’s rules do not allow it, as set out in section 12. We may change or
retire parts of the Platform.

4. Your account and using the Platform
4.1 Sign-up. Opening an account is free. We ask for your name, email, business name
and address, and anything else we need to review your application. Keep your details
accurate and up to date.

4.2 Age and authority. You must be 18 or over and able to enter into a binding
contract.

4.3 Security. Keep your login private. You are responsible for what happens under your
account.

4.4 Your Content. You are responsible for everything you upload or send. You confirm
that you own it or have the right to use it, that it is accurate, and that it follows our Listing
Guidelines and Acceptable Use Rules.

4.5 Messages, contact details and links. Guests contact you through the Platform’s
messaging, and Messages are stored. Do not put websites, links of any kind, email
addresses, phone numbers or social links in your Listing, images or Messages before a
booking is made. This includes links to your venue or its website. We may remove them.
We show your display name and a short bio publicly, and your trading name and
address at checkout, as the law requires.

4.6 Third-party tools. The Platform may link to or work with third-party tools, including
Stripe. We do not control them and are not responsible for them.

5. Listing and selling your retreat
How payments work, and why. We’ve kept this as simple as we can. When a guest
books, they pay on our website straight into your own Stripe account. Our 15%
commission comes out of that first payment automatically, and that’s the end of our part.
There are no invoices, no chasing and no back and forth between us. Everything that
lands in your account after that is yours, and you collect the balance from your guest in
whatever way suits you. It also means you have money early for your venue and
supplier deposits.


5.1 Who can list. You must be 18 or over, legally allowed to run the retreat you list, and
able to enter into a contract. Where you act for a business, you confirm you have
authority to bind it.

5.2 Registration and review. After you open an account and complete the retreat
application form, we review the retreat against the Listing Guidelines. We may approve
it, ask for more information, or decline it.

5.3 Your Listing. Keep it accurate and complete. It must show the dates, location,
length, Ticket Price, what is included and excluded, who leads the retreat, your balance
due date, your cancellation policy, and any physical, health, age or safety information a
Guest would reasonably need. You may also choose to state a minimum number of
Guests needed for the retreat to run, and the date by which you will confirm it
goes ahead. This is optional. If you would like it shown on your Listing, please tell
us. If the minimum is not reached and you cancel, clause 5.17 applies. Update it
promptly when something changes. We may tidy titles, grammar and layout, but we will
not change its meaning or price without your agreement.

5.3A Your venue. You are welcome to name and describe the venue where your retreat
is held, and to show photos of it, as part of your Listing. Only use venue photos you
have permission to use, such as photos the venue has agreed you may use. Your
Listing must not include a link to the venue, its website or any other website,
whether or not the venue is listed on the Platform (clause 4.5). Keep the venue details
accurate, and update them if the venue changes.

5.4 You are the seller. You are responsible for delivering the retreat as described. That
includes licences and permits, insurance, safeguarding, health and safety, risk
assessments, using suitably qualified people, medical screening where appropriate, your
suppliers, local laws and your taxes.

5.5 Insurance. We do not list any retreat without proper insurance. Before your first
Listing goes live, you must send us proof that you hold, for each retreat:
  •   public liability insurance (liability or indemnity cover) appropriate to your retreat
      and the country where it takes place; and
  •   cover for cancelling or postponing your retreat, such as event cancellation
      insurance, so that you can refund Guests if something goes wrong.

Where they apply, you must also hold tour operator insurance and professional
indemnity insurance for the services you provide. Keep your cover in force until the
retreat has ended and every Guest has been served or refunded, and send us updated
proof when it renews. Please check what your policy covers: many policies do not cover
a retreat cancelled because too few places have sold. If your cover lapses, we may hide
your Listing until you send new proof. Payments you make to venues, chefs, excursions
and other suppliers are your risk and never our responsibility.

5.6 Lawful retreats and substances. You confirm that your retreat, including every
activity, practice and substance, is lawful in the country where it takes place, and that
you hold any licence or permission required. You must not supply or allow any
substance that is illegal there. If your retreat includes plant medicine, kava or any other
substance whose legal status varies between countries, you must declare it on the
application form and confirm that it is lawful where the retreat takes place. Light Path
Retreats has no involvement in any substance offered at a retreat and takes no
responsibility for it. If we believe a retreat breaks the law, these Terms or our Listing
Guidelines, we may suspend the Listing or your account with immediate effect.

5.7 Package travel. If the law where you sell treats your retreat as a package holiday or
other regulated travel product, you are responsible for complying with it, including any
insolvency protection and tour operator insurance.

5.8 Founding Offer. The first 500 retreat Listings registered before 31 December 2026
receive a Bronze membership free throughout 2027. If you choose Silver or Gold
instead, you pay that tier’s price from the start. Our Commission still applies to every
booking during the free year. From 2028 the Bronze price shown on our website applies,
and we will give you at least 30 days’ notice before it starts. We may extend or shorten
the registration period for sign-ups not yet made. The Founding Offer lasts only while
your account is in good standing.



Please read this part carefully before you accept
We want you to go in with your eyes open. These are the points that matter most. The
full detail is in clauses 5.5 and 5.9 to 5.19.
1. You are the seller and the merchant of record. You connect your own Stripe
account, and Guest payments go into it.
2. Our Commission is 15% of the full Ticket Price, taken automatically from the
Guest’s first payment the moment they book.
3. Booked more than 6 weeks ahead: the Guest pays a 40% Retainer, or the full price
where clause 5.11 says so, and may cancel within 72 hours. After that, the Retainer is
non-refundable. We then return our Commission to you less €30, and the Guest’s
Cancellation Charge covers the card costs, so you are not out of pocket.
4. Booked 6 weeks or less ahead: the Guest pays the full price, and the whole
amount is non-refundable from the moment of booking. Our Commission is never
returned. If you choose to give a goodwill refund, you pay our Commission and the card
fees yourself.
5. After the 72 hours, our Commission is kept in every case, including if the Guest
does not pay the balance or does not attend.
6. If you cancel or postpone a retreat or a Guest cannot make a postponed date, you
refund the Guest in full within 14 days. Our Commission is kept in every case. A €150
fee applies to a cancellation, unless you postpone to a confirmed new date or a serious
event outside your control is backed by evidence.
7. Chargebacks are raised against your Stripe account, and you carry them.
8. Insurance is required. Before your retreat goes live, you send us proof of liability
insurance and cover for cancelling or postponing.



5.9 Connecting your Stripe Account. By accepting these Terms, you agree to connect
your own Stripe Account to Light Path Retreats through the Platform before your first
Listing goes live. You must keep it connected and in good standing while you have a live
Listing. You accept Stripe’s Connected Account Agreement and complete Stripe’s
identity and business checks. We never see or hold your Stripe login.

Your business must be registered in a country where Stripe is available. We cannot
accept retreats from planners who are unable to connect a Stripe account. If your
Stripe Account is disconnected, restricted or closed, your Listings are hidden until it is
restored.

5.10 Commission and what it covers. For every place booked through the Platform,
you pay us a Commission of 15% of the full Ticket Price. The Commission is our fee for:
  •    listing and showing your retreat on the Platform;
  •    promoting the Platform and its Listings, which may include featuring your retreat
       on our social media, in newsletters and in other channels we choose; and
  •    taking the Booking Payment for you through our checkout.

The Commission does not depend on how much promotion a particular retreat receives,
and we do not promise any number of views, enquiries or bookings. Your Membership is
separate and paid for separately (section 6).

5.11 The Booking Payment. When a Guest books, they pay through the Platform into
your Stripe Account:
  •    a Retainer of 40% of the Ticket Price, non-refundable once the Cancellation
       Window has closed, if they book more than 6 weeks before the start date, the
       Ticket Price is €300 or more, and you have not chosen Full Payment; or
  •    the Full Payment of 100% of the Ticket Price, in any of these cases: (a) they
       book 6 weeks or less before the start date; (b) the Ticket Price is under €300, for
       example a one-day or short event; or (c) you have chosen, when listing the
       retreat, to take the full price at booking. Your choice of payment option is shown
       on your Listing before the Guest books.

The 6 weeks are counted back from the start date. For a retreat starting on 10 April,
anyone booking on or after 27 February pays in full.

5.12 How the Commission is taken. You authorise us to instruct Stripe to deduct the
full Commission from each Booking Payment as a platform fee at the moment the Guest
pays. Stripe’s card and currency fees are charged to your Stripe Account by Stripe, at
Stripe’s rates. You receive the rest on your Stripe payout schedule. Whether the
Booking Payment is a Retainer or the full price, the whole Commission, 15% of the full
Ticket Price, is taken from it. The Commission is earned when the booking is made.

5.13 The balance. You collect the balance of the Ticket Price directly from the Guest, by
a due date you set and show on your Listing. You send your own reminders and keep
track of your own deadlines. We take no part in collecting the balance. The Commission
is not reduced or returned if the Guest pays late, pays less, never pays the balance or
does not attend, or if you choose to give a refund. The only exception is a cancellation
within the Cancellation Window (clause 5.14).

5.13A What carries Commission, and changes after booking. Our Commission
applies to the Ticket Price: everything included for every Guest, the room type chosen,
and any transfer or other retreat option you offer through the Platform. Anything every
Guest receives must be included in the Ticket Price and not sold as an extra.

Optional treatments and activities that not every Guest takes, such as massages or
private sessions, and extra nights or travel outside the retreat dates, do not carry
Commission. You arrange and charge for these directly with the Guest.

Our Commission is calculated on the Ticket Price at checkout. It is not reduced if the
Guest later moves to a cheaper option, or if you give them a discount or partial refund. If
a Guest upgrades their room or adds a transfer after booking, please make the change
through the Platform. Commission is then due on the extra amount, invoiced to you and
payable within 14 days.

Cancellations: important, please read
5.14 The 72-hour Cancellation Window (bookings made more than 6 weeks
ahead). A Guest who books more than 6 weeks before the start date may cancel
through the Platform within 72 hours of booking, or up to 24 hours before the start
date if that comes first. When they do, you authorise us to do the following
automatically, and you do not need to take any action:
  •   refund the Guest from your Stripe Account the Booking Payment they paid,
      whether a Retainer or the full price, less a Cancellation Charge of €30 plus the
      actual card processing costs of their payment; and
  •   return our Commission to your Stripe Account, less €30, which we keep for
      handling the cancellation.

Stripe does not return its fees on a refund. The Guest’s Cancellation Charge
covers them, so you are not out of pocket. Until the Cancellation Window closes,
keep enough in your Stripe Account to cover a refund. If your balance is too low when a
refund is due, Stripe may recover the shortfall from your bank account.

5.15 Bookings made 6 weeks or less before the start. The Guest pays the full
Ticket Price at booking, and the whole amount is non-refundable from the moment
the booking is made. The Cancellation Window does not apply, and our Commission is
never returned. A place given up this close to the start is very hard to fill again. If you
nevertheless choose to give a Guest a refund as a goodwill gesture, you fund it
entirely yourself, including the part that paid our Commission and Stripe’s fees.

5.16 After the Cancellation Window. Our Commission is non-refundable in every
circumstance, including where the Guest cancels, does not attend or does not pay the
balance, and where you cancel or change the retreat. Any refund after the Cancellation
Window is between you and the Guest under your cancellation policy. You issue it
yourself, and we do not process it.

5.17 If you cancel a retreat. You must refund every Guest in full, within 14 days,
for everything they have paid, including the part of the Booking Payment that paid
our Commission. You must tell us before you tell your Guests. Our Commission is
kept in every case, whatever the reason for the cancellation, because the promotion
and booking work have already been done. This is one of the reasons we require
insurance (clause 5.5). You remain responsible for any costs you owe to suppliers.
Repeated or late cancellations may lead to suspension or removal from the Platform.

5.17A Planner cancellation fee. We also charge a fee of €150 if you cancel a retreat
on which at least one place has been booked through the Platform. It covers the
promotion we have already put into your retreat and the support we give your Guests
through the cancellation, including answering their questions, checking their refunds and
helping them find another retreat. It is invoiced and due within 14 days. Cancelling
because too few places have sold is not a reason to waive the fee. We waive it only:
  •   if you postpone the retreat to a confirmed new date (clause 5.17B); or
  •   if the cancellation is caused by a serious event outside your control, such as a
      death in your close family, serious illness, the loss of the venue (for example
      through fire or flood), natural disaster, war or a government travel ban, and you
      send us reasonable evidence within 14 days. We will consider the evidence
      fairly and in confidence.

5.17B Postponing a retreat. If you move a retreat to a new date, you must confirm the
new date, tell your Guests directly and update your Listing. Guests who can attend the
new date keep their booking. Any Guest who cannot attend must be refunded in full
by you within 14 days. Our Commission is kept, because the promotion and
booking work have been done. No planner cancellation fee applies.

5.17C Help finding another venue. If your venue becomes unavailable, we will do our
best to help, for example by sharing your dates with the Venues on our Platform, so that
you may be able to change venue instead of cancelling or postponing. This is goodwill
support, not a promise of a result.

Protecting both of us
5.18 Chargebacks and disputes. Because you are the merchant of record, any
chargeback or payment dispute is raised against your Stripe Account. You respond to it,
and you carry the disputed amount, the fees and any penalties.

5.19 Recovering money from you. If Stripe, a card scheme or a bank takes any
amount from Light Path Retreats in connection with your retreat, you will repay it within
14 days of our invoice. This includes a chargeback, a dispute fee, our Commission or a
refund you failed to make. Until you repay it, we may suspend your account and hide
your Listings. This clause continues after your account closes.

5.20 No steering, and no avoiding the Commission. If a Guest contacts you through
the Platform, you must keep that booking on the Platform. You are not responsible if a
Guest decides, on their own, to book somewhere else. Do not ask, encourage or help
Guests who found you through the Platform to book or pay somewhere else. Do not
share links or contact details for that purpose, ask a Guest to cancel and rebook directly,
or split a price to reduce the Commission. If you do, the Commission is due on the full
Ticket Price, and we may remove your Listings and close your account.

5.20A Best price, like for like. The price of your retreat on Light Path Retreats
must never be higher than the price you offer for the same place anywhere else,
including on your own website, on other platforms, and in emails, newsletters, messages
or social media. “The same place” means the same retreat, dates, room type and
inclusions. You must not make a retreat look cheaper elsewhere by leaving out
something that is included on Light Path Retreats, such as a transfer or meals.

5.20B Changing your price, early birds and other offers. You are free to change your
price whenever you like, for example to run an early bird offer, to give a discount for
paying in full, or to reduce the price nearer the start date. Every price change and
every offer must also be made on Light Path Retreats, on the same terms and
dates, at the same time as you make it anywhere else. Update your Listing, or ask us
to, before or at the moment the new price goes live elsewhere, and before you send it to
your own mailing list or contacts. Early bird and other time-limited offers are shown on
your Listing with the offer price, the full price and the date the offer ends. When the offer
ends, you may raise the price again in the same way. If you offer a discount for paying in
full, Guests booking through Light Path Retreats must be able to take it too, paying the
full Ticket Price through the Platform.

5.20C Where else you sell. When you list a retreat, tell us where else it is sold, and
keep us informed if that changes. We may check prices and offers on other websites
and channels.

5.20D If your retreat is cheaper elsewhere. Offering a lower price elsewhere, or an
offer not available on Light Path Retreats, is a breach of these Terms. If it happens:
  •    our Commission is kept, calculated on the Ticket Price at checkout;
  •    if a Guest who booked through us asks for the lower price, it is yours to resolve
       with them, at your own cost, for example by giving them the difference against the
       balance. We are not involved and do not refund any Commission; and
  •    we will usually give you a written warning first. A further breach, or a serious one,
       may lead us to suspend your Listings or end our agreement with you under
       section 12.

We ask this because Guests should be able to trust that booking through Light Path
Retreats is never a worse deal. If you sell in several places, keeping one price
everywhere is also the simplest way to avoid Guests cancelling in one place to rebook in
another.

5.21 Your cancellation policy. Our standard policy is simple: after the Cancellation
Window the Booking Payment is non-refundable, and a booking made 6 weeks or
less before the start is non-refundable from the moment it is made. You may
choose to offer Guests a more generous policy of your own, for example a partial refund
up to a certain date. If you do, write it in full on your Listing, apply it as written, and fund
any refund yourself. Our Commission is not returned (clauses 5.15 and 5.16).

5.21A Selling elsewhere, and places left. You are free to sell your retreat on your own
website and on other platforms as well as on Light Path Retreats. Because we cannot
see bookings made elsewhere, every retreat Listing carries a “places left” count that you
set and manage. It can be all the places on your retreat, or only the number you choose
to sell through Light Path Retreats. When it reaches zero, the Platform stops taking
bookings, and we may show the count on your Listing.

You must keep us up to date with your availability at all times. Whenever a place is
booked anywhere else, on your own website, on another platform or directly, or a Guest
drops out, update the count straight away. We rely entirely on the count you give us.
We are not responsible for any overbooking, refund or loss that results from it
being out of date. Any such loss is yours. If a retreat is oversold, you must offer the
affected Guest a place on another date or a full refund, at your own cost, and our
Commission is kept. You will also cover any cost or claim we face because of it (section
14). Repeated overselling may lead to your Listing or account being suspended.

5.22 Replying to Guests. Reply to Messages promptly, and within two business days.

5.23 Good standing. The Founding Offer and any other special terms last only while
your account is in good standing.

6. Membership: Bronze, Silver and Gold
6.1 Bronze, per Listing. Every Listing needs at least a Bronze membership to appear
on the Platform. Membership is per Listing, because we promote each retreat on its
own: a Planner with five retreats pays for five memberships. Bronze costs €12.22 a
month, or €122.22 a year, and includes the basic promotion described on our website. It
renews automatically until you cancel. Founding Planners receive Bronze free in 2027
(clause 5.8).

6.1A Paying yearly. If you pay for a full year, you pay for ten months and receive
twelve, a saving of about 17%. In return, a yearly membership is a commitment for
the full year and is not refundable, even if you remove the Listing or close your
account before the year ends.

6.2 Silver and Gold. If you would like more promotion, you can choose Silver or Gold.
You pay the price of the tier you choose, instead of the Bronze price, not on top of it.
Silver and Gold are billed monthly. What each tier includes, and its current price, are
shown on our website, and the price shown when you choose a tier applies.

6.3 Changing tier. To move up or down a tier, give us at least 14 days’ written notice
before your next monthly renewal date, by email or in your account. The change then
takes effect from that renewal. If you give less than 14 days’ notice, you are charged one
more month at your current tier, and the change takes effect from the renewal after that.
If you stop Silver or Gold, your membership returns to Bronze.

6.4 Cancelling your membership. You can cancel a monthly membership at any time
in your account, and it ends at the end of the month you have paid for. For a yearly
membership, you can give notice to cancel at any time during the year, in your account
or by email. Your notice must reach us at least 30 days before your renewal date. If
it does not, your yearly membership renews automatically for another year, and
that year is not refundable. A yearly membership runs to the end of the year you have
paid for, with no refund (clause 6.1A). For example, if your year runs from 1 April to 31
March and you give notice in September, your Listing stays live until 31 March and does
not renew, as long as your notice reaches us by 1 March. When a membership ends,
the Listing is hidden. Planners must still honour confirmed bookings (clause 12.1).

6.5 No refunds. Work starts as soon as you join or move up a tier and a team is
assigned, so membership fees are not refundable, including for a period already started.

6.6 How Listings are shown, and promotion. Listings appear in search results
according to what the Guest searches for, such as dates, country, type of retreat and
price. Silver and Gold Listings may be shown more prominently, in featured places and
on our homepage, and paid placement is always labelled “Featured”. We may change
how Listings are ordered to improve the Platform, and we will explain the main factors
on our website. We choose dates and channels, working with you where we can. We do
not promise any number of views, inquiries or bookings. Material you give us must be
accurate and lawful, and we may decline or amend promotional content that does not
follow these Terms.

6.7 Paying, reminders and missed payments. Membership is paid by recurring card
payment. For a yearly membership, we send you a reminder at least 45 days before
each renewal date, so you have time to decide before the 30-day notice deadline in
clause 6.4. For a monthly membership, we send you a reminder before each payment is

12. Suspending and ending an account
12.1 You can close your account at any time. Planners must first honour confirmed

12.2 We may suspend or close an account or remove a Listing if we reasonably believe

15. Changes to these Terms
15.1 We may update these Terms. We post the new version on the Platform and email
registered Planners at least 30 days before it takes effect. If you keep using the Platform
after that date, you accept the update. If you do not accept it, you can close your
account before it starts. Changes do not affect bookings already made or a Founding
Offer during its stated period.

16. General
16.1 Notices. We contact you by email at the address on your account or through the
Platform. You can reach us at connect@lightpathretreats.com. An email is treated as
received on the next business day.

16.2 Complaints. If you are unhappy with a decision we have made about your account

Schedule A: Listing Guidelines
A1. All Listings
  •   Be honest and specific. Say what is included, what is not, and what a Guest can
      expect.
  •   Do not make medical claims. Never promise to cure, treat or prevent a medical
      condition.
  •   Show real prices in the currency stated, with any extras clearly separate.
  •   Do not list anything unlawful or unsafe, and do not use anyone else’s name,
      photos or reviews without permission.
  •   Do not include links of any kind, websites, email addresses, phone numbers or
      social links. This includes links to your venue or its website.
  •   Keep availability and details current.

A2. Images and video
  •   Full-colour, clear, landscape photos. Suggested size 1600 by 900 pixels.
  •   Your own images, or ones you have the right to use, including photos of your
      venue.
  •   One scene per image. No collages, superimposed text or watermarks. A small,
      discreet logo is fine, as long as it does not show a website address.
  •   No website addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, social media handles
      or QR codes in any image or video.
  •   No nudity.
  •   Images must show the real place, people and facilities.
  •   We check images when we review a Listing and when new images are added,

  •   Dates, location, length, and what is included and excluded.

Schedule B: Acceptable Use Rules
  •    Follow the law wherever you are and wherever your retreat takes place.
  •    Be truthful. Do not give false information, impersonate anyone, or create fake
       accounts or reviews.
  •    Treat others with respect. No harassment, abuse, discrimination or threats.
  •    No spam. Do not send unsolicited bulk messages or use Message details for
       marketing without consent.
  •    Do not scrape, copy or harvest data from the Platform by automated means.
  •    Do not interfere with the Platform, test its security without permission, or upload
       malware.
  •    Do not avoid our Commission or fees, including by steering Guests off the
       Platform or hiding bookings.
  •    Do not try to influence reviews unfairly.
  •    Respect privacy. Use other people’s information only for the purpose it was given.

If you see something that breaks these rules, tell us at
connect@lightpathretreats.com. We will look into it and may remove content or close
an account.

Schedule C: Copyright notices
If you believe in good faith that material on the Platform infringes your copyright, email a
notice to connect@lightpathretreats.com that includes:

  •   your name, postal address, email address and telephone number; and
  •   your signature, physical or electronic.

We process complete notices only. Giving false information in a notice may make you
liable for damages. If we remove content, we tell the person who posted it, and they may
send us a response.

1. Welcome and who we are
 Light Path Retreats is a marketing platform that helps retreat planners find the right
 place for their retreats. We list and promote your venue. We take no commission
 on any booking you make, and the booking is always between you and the
 planner.


1.1 These Venue Terms ("Terms") are an agreement between you and Light Path
Retreats LLC, a limited liability company registered in New Mexico, USA, of 1209
Mountain Road Pl NE, Ste R, Albuquerque, NM 87110, USA ("Light Path", "we", "us"
or "our"). They apply to owners and managers of retreat venues (each a "Venue")
who list a venue on lightpathretreats.com and related services (the "Platform").
1.2 By creating an account and ticking the box that says you have read and agree to
these Terms, you accept them. If you accept for a business, you confirm that you
have authority to bind it. We keep a record of the date, time and version you
accepted.
1.3 Retreat planners and facilitators who use the Platform have their own separate
terms. If you also run your own retreats or offer your services as a facilitator, those
terms apply to that part of what you do.
1.4 These Terms form one agreement with the Venue Listing Guidelines and
approval criteria (Schedule A), the Acceptable Use Rules (Schedule B), the copyright
notice process (Schedule C), and our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy, both
published on our website. If they disagree, these Terms come first, then the
Schedules, then the policies.

2. Words we use
 Word                   Meaning

 Venue                  A person or business that owns or manages a retreat venue
                        and lists it on the Platform.

 Venue Listing          Your venue page on the Platform. Each approved venue
                        has its own Venue Listing.

 Planner                A retreat planner or retreat leader who uses the Platform to
                        plan, list or sell retreats, and who may contact you about
                        hosting one.

                        inquiry form or messaging.

                        paid, and each 12 months after that while it renews.

                        same calendar date your Membership Year began.

                        section 9.

 Content                Anything you upload, submit or send through the Platform,
                        including text, images, video and messages.



3. What we do, and what we do not do
3.1 We run a marketing platform. We provide your Venue Listing, a way for Planners
to send you Inquiries, promotion of the Platform and of Venue Listings as described
in section 8, and regular figures on how your Venue Listing is doing.
3.2 We take no commission. We do not charge any commission or booking fee on
any booking you make with a Planner or anyone else, whether or not they found you
through the Platform. Your Membership is the only fee you pay us.
3.3 We are not a party to any agreement between you and a Planner, a guest or
anyone else. Availability, prices, contracts, deposits, payments, cancellations and
refunds for your venue are agreed directly between you and the Planner. We do not
take, hold or process any payment for a venue booking.

3.4 We do not own, run, inspect, supervise or insure any venue, and we do not
organise or run retreats. We are not responsible for what happens at your venue,
including accommodation, food, facilities, activities, health and safety, permits,
licences or insurance. Those are your responsibility as the Venue.
3.5 What "approved" means. When we approve a Venue Listing, we have
checked your application against our approval criteria (Schedule A) on the
information and photos you gave us. Approval is not an inspection, a visit, a rating or
a guarantee of your venue, its safety or its suitability for any retreat.
3.6 We may decline, hide or remove any Venue Listing at our discretion, including
where a payment provider’s rules do not allow it, as set out in sections 5 and 15. We
may change or retire parts of the Platform.


4. Your account and using the Platform
4.1 Sign-up. Opening an account is free. We ask for your name, email, business
name and address, and anything else we need to review your application. Keep your
details accurate and up to date.
4.2 Age and authority. You must be 18 or over and able to enter into a binding
contract. You must own the venue, or be authorised by its owner to list and market it.
4.3 Security. Keep your login private. You are responsible for what happens under
your account.
4.4 Your Content. You are responsible for everything you upload or send. You
confirm that you own it or have the right to use it, that it is accurate, and that it
follows the Venue Listing Guidelines and Acceptable Use Rules.
4.5 Third-party tools. The Platform may link to or work with third-party tools,
including Stripe, our payment provider. We do not control them and are not
responsible for them.


5. Applying and being approved
5.1 Applying. Open an account and complete the venue application form. We
review each application against the approval criteria in Schedule A and tell you our
decision. We may ask for more photos, documents or information.
5.2 Our decision. We may approve an application, ask for more information, or
decline it. We may decline an application that does not meet the approval criteria, or
where we reasonably believe the venue is not a good fit for the Platform. Where we
decline, we will tell you why.
5.3 Holiday homes. Holiday homes are not accepted. By this we mean properties
let mainly to families or individuals for holidays, without the group space and facilities
needed to host a retreat.

5.4 Lawful venues and substances. You confirm that your venue, and every
activity, practice and service you offer there, is lawful in the country where the venue
is. You must not supply or allow any substance that is illegal there. If your venue
offers plant medicine, kava or any other substance whose legal status varies
between countries, you must declare it on the application form. We do not list venues
whose services include substances or products that our payment provider does not
allow, and we may decline or remove a Venue Listing for that reason.
5.5 Permits and licences. You are responsible for holding every permit, licence
and registration your venue needs to host guests and groups, including for
accommodation, food and drink, and events, and for following local law, including
health and safety, fire safety, food hygiene, accessibility and tourist taxes.
5.6 Insurance. We do not require proof of insurance before your Venue Listing goes
live, but we strongly recommend that you hold public liability insurance and
any other cover appropriate to your venue and the country where it is. Planners
may ask you about your insurance before booking. Insurance is a matter between
you, your insurer and the Planner, and we are not responsible for it.
5.7 Several venues. Each venue is reviewed and approved on its own. A Gold
Membership covers up to five venues (clause 8.4), and each of them must be
approved before its Venue Listing goes live.


6. Your Venue Listing
6.1 What your Venue Listing shows. Your Venue Listing shows your venue’s
name and location, photos, description, sleeping capacity and rooms, group and
outdoor spaces, catering, accessibility, a price guide, and anything else a Planner
would reasonably need to decide whether to contact you. Schedule A sets out what
we ask for.
6.2 Keeping it accurate. Keep your Venue Listing accurate and complete, and
update it promptly when something changes, such as your capacity, facilities, price
guide or photos. A Venue Listing that is materially out of date or misleading may be
hidden until it is corrected.
6.3 Availability. We do not show or manage your availability. Planners ask you
about dates directly, and availability and prices are agreed between you and the
Planner.
6.4 Your venue’s name. Your Venue Listing shows your venue’s real name, so that
Planners can research it, look at reviews and arrange a visit. Your direct contact
details, such as phone numbers, email addresses and websites, are not shown on
your Venue Listing (section 7).
6.5 Retreats held at your venue. Planners holding a retreat at your venue may
name and describe your venue in their retreat listing, and show photos of it with your
permission. Retreat listings do not link to Venue Listings or to any other website.

You agree that Planners may refer to your venue by name in this way. If you believe
a retreat listing describes your venue inaccurately, tell us and we will look into it.
6.6 How Venue Listings are shown. Venue Listings appear in search results
according to what the person searching asks for, such as country, capacity, style and
facilities. Silver and Gold Venue Listings may be shown more prominently, in
featured places and on our homepage, and paid placement is always labelled
"Featured". We may change how listings are ordered to improve the Platform, and
we will explain the main factors on our website.
6.7 Tidying your Listing. We may tidy titles, grammar and layout, but we will not
change the meaning of your Venue Listing without your agreement.


7. Inquiries and your dealings with Planners
7.1 How Planners contact you. Planners and others contact you through the
Platform’s inquiry form. Inquiries reach you by email and in your account, and we
keep a record of them so that we can show you how many views and Inquiries your
Venue Listing receives.
7.2 Replying. Please reply to Inquiries promptly, and within two business days.
Repeated failure to reply may affect how your Venue Listing is shown.
7.3 After the first contact. Once a Planner has contacted you, you are free to
continue the conversation directly, by email, phone or a visit, and to agree a booking
in whatever way suits you. We take no commission on that booking (clause 3.2).
7.4 Your booking with a Planner. Your contract with a Planner is yours. You set
your own prices, deposits, payment terms and cancellation policy, and you deal
directly with the Planner on everything to do with the booking, including any dispute.
We are not involved and cannot help to enforce it.
7.5 Venues falling through. If a Planner’s venue becomes unavailable, we may
share the Planner’s dates and needs with Venues on the Platform, to help them find
a replacement. This is goodwill support, not a promise that you will receive any such
request.

  Please read this part carefully before you accept
  We want you to go in with your eyes open. These are the points about money
  that matter most. The full detail is in sections 8 to 10.

  1. We take no commission. You keep everything you earn from every booking,
  however the Planner found you.

  2. You pay a yearly Membership for each venue, in advance, by credit or debit
  card: Bronze €199, Silver €499, or Gold €1,190 for up to five venues.

3. Membership is yearly only. Your Membership Year starts on the day you pay
  and renews automatically on the same date each year.

  4. Cancel at least 30 days before your Renewal Date, or your Membership
  renews for another year. You can give notice at any time during the year, and
  your Venue Listing stays live until the year you paid for ends. We remind you 45
  days before each renewal.

  5. Membership is not refundable, including if you remove your Venue Listing or
  close your account part-way through a Membership Year.

  6. Founding Offer: the first 100 approved Venues get Bronze free until 31
  March 2027. Your first yearly payment is taken on 1 April 2027. We remind you
  by 15 February 2027, and you can cancel free of charge by 1 March 2027.

  7. If a payment fails, you have 3 days to pay. Promotion is paused during those
  days, and after that your Venue Listing is hidden until you pay.

  8. We promote your venue, but we cannot promise any number of views,
  Inquiries or bookings.



8. Membership: Bronze, Silver and Gold
8.1 Membership is needed to be listed. Every approved venue needs a
Membership to appear on the Platform. Membership is per venue: a Venue with two
venues needs two Bronze or Silver Memberships, or one Gold Membership.
8.2 Bronze, €199 a year, one venue. Your Venue Listing, Inquiries from Planners
through the Platform, and a regular report of the views and Inquiries your Venue
Listing receives.
8.3 Silver, €499 a year, one venue. Everything in Bronze, plus:
 • a "Featured" badge and a featured place on our homepage and in search results;
 • features in our newsletter to retreat planners, such as "Venue of the month";
 • posts about your venue on our social media channels;
 • a venue spotlight in our blog and education content;
 • priority when Planners ask us to suggest venues; and
 • your Venue Listing published within 24 hours of approval.


8.4 Gold, €1,190 a year, up to five venues. Everything in Silver, for up to five
approved venues owned or managed by the same Venue. It is designed for hotel
groups, estates and property managers. Each venue covered must be approved
under section 5.

8.5 Promotion. We choose the dates, channels and wording of promotion, working
with you where we can, and we aim to share the promotion fairly between Venues on
the same tier. What each tier includes is also shown on our website. We do not
promise any number of views, Inquiries or bookings. Material you give us must be
accurate and lawful, and we may decline or amend promotional content that does
not follow these Terms.
8.6 Yearly only. Membership is paid once a year, in advance. There is no
monthly option. A yearly Membership is a commitment for the full Membership
Year.
8.7 When your Membership Year starts. Your Membership Year starts on the day
your Membership is paid, and your Venue Listing goes live once your venue is
approved and your Membership is in place. For Venues in the Founding Offer, the
first paid Membership Year starts on 1 April 2027 (section 9).
8.8 Automatic renewal. Your Membership renews automatically on your Renewal
Date each year, at the price shown on our website at that time, until you cancel. We
send you a reminder at least 45 days before each Renewal Date, with the
amount that will be taken, so you have time to decide before the cancellation
deadline in clause 8.11.
8.9 Moving up a tier. You can move up to a higher tier at any time during your
Membership Year. You pay the difference between the two tiers for the rest of your
Membership Year, and your Renewal Date stays the same. The new tier starts as
soon as you pay.
8.10 Moving down a tier. To move down a tier, tell us by email or in your account
at least 30 days before your Renewal Date. The change takes effect from that
Renewal Date, and the lower price applies from then.
8.11 Cancelling. You can give notice to cancel at any time during your Membership
Year, in your account or by email. Your notice must reach us at least 30 days
before your Renewal Date. If it does not, your Membership renews
automatically for another year, and that year is not refundable. Your Venue
Listing stays live until the end of the Membership Year you have paid for, and is then
hidden. For example, if your Membership Year runs from 1 April to 31 March and you

Schedule A: Venue Listing Guidelines and approval
criteria
A1. Approval criteria
We look for venues that can genuinely host a group retreat. We review each
application against these criteria:
 • Around four or more bedrooms, or several properties that can be booked
   together for one group.
 • An indoor room where the whole group can gather, and outdoor space.
 • A usable kitchen or catering for the group. Hotels are welcome.
 • Willingness to host group retreats.
 • Your own website, and photos and details that accurately show the venue.
 • Any permits and licences the venue needs to host guests and groups (clause
   5.5).


Not accepted: holiday homes (clause 5.3), and venues whose services include
substances or products that are unlawful where the venue is, or that our payment
provider does not allow (clause 5.4).
Approval is based on the information you provide. It is not an inspection (clause 3.5).
A2. All Venue Listings
 • Be honest and specific. Describe the venue as it really is, including anything a
   group would need to know.
 • Do not make medical claims. Never promise that a stay will cure, treat or prevent
   a medical condition.
 • Give a realistic price guide in the currency stated, and say what it includes.
 • Do not list anything unlawful or unsafe, and do not use anyone else’s name,
   photos or reviews.
 • Do not include links of any kind, websites, email addresses, phone numbers,
   social links or QR codes in your Venue Listing, images or video.


A3. What to include
 • Venue name, country and nearest town, and how guests usually travel there.
 • Sleeping capacity, number and type of rooms, and bathrooms.
 • Group room or practice space, its size and what it is suitable for.
 • Outdoor space and setting.
 • Catering: self-catering kitchen, in-house catering, or both, and dietary options.
 • Accessibility, and anything that may limit who can stay.

• A price guide, for example per night or per week for the whole venue, and any
   minimum stay.
 • Any plant medicine or other substance whose legal status varies, with its legal
   basis (clause 5.4).


A4. Images and video
 • Full-colour, clear, landscape photos. Suggested size 1600 by 900 pixels.
 • Your own images, or ones you have the right to use.
 • One scene per image. No collages, superimposed text or watermarks. A small,
   discreet logo is fine.
 • No nudity.
 • Images must show the real venue, rooms and facilities as they are now.



Schedule B: Acceptable Use Rules
 • Follow the law wherever you are and wherever your venue is.
 • Be truthful. Do not give false information, impersonate anyone, or create fake
   accounts or reviews.
 • Treat others with respect. No harassment, abuse, discrimination or threats.
 • No spam. Do not send unsolicited bulk messages or use Inquiry details for
   marketing without consent.
 • Do not scrape, copy or harvest data from the Platform by automated means.
 • Do not interfere with the Platform, test its security without permission, or upload
   malware.
 • Do not try to influence reviews unfairly.
 • Respect privacy. Use other people’s information only for the purpose it was

If you see something that breaks these rules, tell us at
connect@lightpathretreats.com. We will look into it and may remove content or
close an account.


Schedule C: Copyright notices

email a notice to connect@lightpathretreats.com that includes:

• a statement that you believe in good faith the use is not authorised by the

 • your signature, physical or electronic.


We process complete notices only. Giving false information in a notice may make
you liable for damages. If we remove content, we tell the person who posted it, and
they may send us a response.

For Facilitators | Version 1.0 | 16 November 2026



1. Welcome and who we are
 Light Path Retreats is a marketing platform. We help retreat planners find the right
 facilitators for their retreats. We take no commission on any booking you receive, and
 your agreement is always directly with the planner.

1.1 These Facilitator Terms (“Terms”) are an agreement between you and Light Path
Retreats LLC, a limited liability company registered in New Mexico, USA, of 1209
Mountain Road Pl NE, Ste R, Albuquerque, NM 87110, USA (“Light Path Retreats”,
“we”, “us” or “our”). They apply to teachers, practitioners, coaches, speakers and other
professionals (each a “Facilitator”) who list their services on lightpathretreats.com and
related services (the “Platform”).
1.2 By creating an account and ticking the box that says you have read and agree to
these Terms, you accept them. If you accept for a business, you confirm that you have
authority to bind it. We keep a record of the date, time and version you accepted.
1.3 Retreat planners and venues who use the Platform have their own separate terms.
If you also run your own retreats or list a venue, those terms apply to that part of what
you do.
1.4 These Terms form one agreement with the Facilitator approval criteria and profile
guidelines (Schedule A), the Acceptable Use Rules (Schedule B), the copyright notice
process (Schedule C), and our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy, both published on our
website. If they disagree, these Terms come first, then the Schedules, then the policies.


2. Words we use
 Word                   Meaning

 Facilitator            A person who offers their skills or services to retreat
                        planners through the Platform, such as a yoga teacher,
                        coach, therapist, breathwork or sound practitioner, chef or
                        speaker.

Word                   Meaning

                        offer and your experience.

 Content                Anything you upload, submit or send through the Platform,
                        including text, images, video and messages.



3. What we do, and what we do not do
3.1 We run a marketing platform. We provide your Profile, a way for Planners to send
you Inquiries, promotion of the Platform and its Profiles, and regular figures on how your
Profile is doing.
3.2 We take no commission. We do not charge any commission or booking fee on
work you receive from a Planner or anyone else, whether or not they found you through
the Platform. Your Membership is the only fee you pay us.
3.3 We are not a party to any agreement between you and a Planner, a guest or
anyone else. Your fees, dates, contracts, payments, cancellations and refunds are
agreed directly between you and the Planner. We do not take, hold or process any
payment for your work.
3.4 We do not supervise, inspect or insure any Facilitator, session or retreat. We are
not responsible for the services you provide or for what happens during them. Those
are your responsibility as the Facilitator.
3.5 What “approved” means. When we approve your Profile, we have checked your
application and your Proof against our approval criteria (Schedule A).

Approval means you passed our review. It is not a guarantee of your skill, your
qualifications, or the quality or safety of any session you deliver.
3.6 We may decline, hide or remove any Profile at our discretion, including where a
payment provider’s rules do not allow it, as set out in sections 5 and 14. We may
change or retire parts of the Platform.


4. Your account and using the Platform
4.1 Sign-up. Opening an account is free. We ask for your name, email, business name
if you have one, address, and anything else we need to review your application. Keep
your details accurate and up to date.
4.2 Age and authority. You must be 18 or over and able to enter into a binding
contract.
4.3 One person, one Profile. Each Profile is for one named person. If several people
work together, each needs their own Profile and Membership.
4.4 Security. Keep your login private. You are responsible for what happens under
your account.
4.5 Your Content. You are responsible for everything you upload or send. You confirm
that you own it or have the right to use it, that it is accurate and truthful, and that it
follows the profile guidelines and Acceptable Use Rules.
4.6 Third-party tools. The Platform may link to or work with third-party tools, including
Stripe, our payment provider. We do not control them and are not responsible for them.


5. Applying and being vetted
 We review every Facilitator individually, because Planners and their guests need to
 trust the people they find here. You do not always need a certificate, but you do need
 to show us that you can deliver what you offer.

5.1 Applying. Open an account and complete the facilitator application form. Tell us
honestly what you offer, how and where you deliver it, and your experience.
5.2 Showing us your experience. With your application, you must give us Proof that
you are who you say you are and that you can deliver what you offer. Proof can include:
 • certificates or qualifications, where your field has them;
 • your own website, or a professional social media or online profile, that we can
   check;
 • references from clients, retreat planners or organisations you have worked with; and
 • examples of your work, such as published articles, recordings, events you have led
   or businesses you have built.

We do not always need a certificate. Real, checkable experience can be enough. But
we must be able to check what you tell us, and you must have at least one place
online, such as a website or professional profile, where we can cross-check your
experience.
5.3 Qualifications. Where your work normally calls for a recognised qualification,
licence or registration, such as yoga or Pilates teaching, massage or bodywork,
counselling, psychotherapy or hypnotherapy, you must hold it and send it to us with
your application. Only claim qualifications and experience you actually hold.
5.4 Insurance. What you need depends on what you do:
 • Insurance required before your Profile goes live. If you work with people’s
   bodies, health, emotions or wellbeing, you must hold public liability insurance and
   professional indemnity insurance appropriate to your work and the countries where
   you work, and send us proof with your application. This includes yoga, Pilates,
   movement, fitness, breathwork, massage and bodywork, coaching, therapy,
   counselling, hypnotherapy, energy and sound healing, cold water or ice work,
   ceremonies, nutrition advice, and guided outdoor or adventure activities.
 • Insurance recommended. If you only share knowledge and experience, for
   example talks or workshops on business, writing, creativity or personal stories,
   insurance is not required, but we strongly recommend it.


We decide which applies when we review your application. If we are unsure, we will ask
for proof of insurance. If your work changes, tell us, and send proof of insurance before
you offer anything that needs it. Keep your insurance in force while your Profile is live,
and send us updated proof when it renews. If your cover lapses, we may hide your
Profile until you send new proof.
5.5 Lawful services and substances. You confirm that everything you offer is lawful
in every country where you offer it, and that you hold any licence or permission
required. If your work involves plant medicine, kava or any other substance whose legal
status varies between countries, you must declare it on the application form and confirm
that it is lawful where you work. We do not list Facilitators whose services include
substances or products that our payment provider does not allow.
5.6 Our decision. We may approve your application, ask for more Proof, or decline it.
We decline where we cannot check what you have told us, where it does not meet our
approval criteria, or where we reasonably believe your services are not a good fit for the
Platform. Where we decline, we will tell you why.
5.7 Checks after approval. We may ask for updated Proof at any time, for example
when your insurance renews or if a concern is raised. If what you told us turns out to be
untrue, we may remove your Profile straight away.

6. Your Profile
6.1 What your Profile shows. Your Profile shows your name and photo, what you
offer, how and where you work (in person, online or both, and the countries you travel
to), your experience and qualifications, a guide to your fees if you wish, and anything
else a Planner would reasonably need to decide whether to contact you. Schedule A
sets out what we ask for.
6.2 Truthful and up to date. You are responsible for everything on your Profile. Fill it
in truthfully and completely, and keep it up to date, including your qualifications,
insurance, services and fees. A Profile that is out of date or misleading may be hidden
until it is corrected.
6.3 Your availability. Keep the availability shown on your Profile up to date, for
example dates or periods when you are fully booked or not working. Planners agree the
final dates with you directly.
6.4 No links or contact details. Your Profile, images and video must not include links
of any kind, websites, email addresses, phone numbers, social media handles or QR
codes. Planners contact you through our inquiry form. The website or online profile you
give us as Proof is used only for our checks and is not shown on your Profile.
6.5 How Profiles are shown. Profiles appear in search results according to what the
person searching asks for, such as skill, location and format. We may change how
Profiles are ordered to improve the Platform, and we will explain the main factors on our
website.
6.6 Tidying your Profile. We may tidy titles, grammar and layout, but we will not
change the meaning of your Profile without your agreement.


7. Inquiries and working with Planners
7.1 How Planners contact you. Planners contact you through the Platform’s inquiry
form. Inquiries reach you by email and in your account, and we keep a record of them
so that we can show you how many views and Inquiries your Profile receives.
7.2 Replying. Please reply to Inquiries promptly, and within two business days.
Repeated failure to reply may affect how your Profile is shown.
7.3 After the first contact. Once a Planner has contacted you, you are free to
continue the conversation directly and to agree your work in whatever way suits you.
We take no commission on it (clause 3.2).
7.4 Your agreement with a Planner. Your agreement with a Planner is yours. You set
your own fees and terms, and you deal directly with the Planner on everything to do with
the work, including any dispute. We are not involved and cannot help to enforce it.
7.5 Caring for guests. You are responsible for delivering your sessions safely and
within your competence. That includes asking about relevant health conditions where
your work calls for it, adapting or stopping a session where needed, and following

safeguarding good practice, especially with vulnerable people. Never make medical
claims or promise to cure, treat or prevent any medical condition.

renews on 1 March and ends on 31 March instead.

least 30 full days before your Renewal Date. If it does not, your Membership
renews automatically for another year, and that year is not refundable. Your Profile
stays live until the end of the year you have paid for.
For example, if your Membership year runs from 1 April to 31 March and you give notice

must reach us by 1 March at the latest, which leaves 30 full days, from 2 March to 31
